bull.b: Very low leverage and substantial equity resources give CG Oncology financial flexibility to fund clinical development without relying immediately on heavy borrowing. This strengthens resilience through upcoming trials and provides capacity to pursue regulatory and commercialization activities.

Progress across a Phase 3 program and published Cohort C results provide meaningful clinical milestones for cretostimogene. These developments can support regulatory filings, improve external validation, and advance the company toward potential commercialization in bladder cancer.

Preserving a key agreement through a favorable legal outcome protects an important element of the company’s existing strategic position. Maintaining contractual rights can reduce disruption to development plans and help preserve future commercial or collaboration opportunities.

bear.b: The company’s cost base remains far larger than its revenue, producing exceptionally deep operating losses and negative gross profit. Until a product is commercialized, this imbalance may persist and require continued funding, increasing the risk of dilution and weaker returns.

Large negative operating and free cash flow show that clinical development currently consumes substantial cash rather than generating it. Continued spending at this level can reduce financial flexibility over time and may require additional financing before durable operating cash generation begins.

Without an approved commercial product, CG Oncology lacks a recurring product-sales base to support ongoing operations. Its dependence on future approvals, collaborations, or financing leaves the business exposed to development outcomes and continued capital-raising requirements.
